examples.english: There are almost no perfect synonyms; in most cases there are differences in nuance.

notes:
A linguistic term for words that share the same or nearly the same meaning. In practice, true synonyms (words with identical meaning in all contexts) are rare; most so-called synonyms differ in register, nuance, or collocational range.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {同義語|どうぎご}⟦{辞典|じてん}→辞典：01640_jiten⟧: thesaurus (synonym dictionary)
- {同義語|どうぎご}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{探|さが}す→探す：00493_sagasu⟧: to look for a synonym
- ⟦{完全|かんぜん}→完全：01552_kanzen⟧な{同義語|どうぎご}: perfect synonym
- {同義語|どうぎご}⟦{関係|かんけい}→関係：01298_kankei⟧: synonymous relationship

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{類義語|るいぎご}→類義語：15939_ruigigo⟧: near-synonym, word with similar meaning (broader term; includes words that are close but not identical in meaning)
- ⟦{対義語|たいぎご}→対義語：29399_taigigo⟧: antonym (word with opposite meaning)
- {類語|るいご}: similar word (casual abbreviation of ⟦{類義語|るいぎご}→類義語：15939_ruigigo⟧)

USAGE:
{同義語|どうぎご} implies words that are interchangeable in most contexts, while ⟦{類義語|るいぎご}→類義語：15939_ruigigo⟧ includes words that are merely similar. In everyday conversation, ⟦{類義語|るいぎご}→類義語：15939_ruigigo⟧ is used more broadly to encompass both categories.
